activities.note: Do three sets of three problems, 45 minutes each, with a short break between sets. Treat them like a real session: a blank file, no notes, no earlier solutions, and only the solving routine and the checker. These problems are original and train patterns, they are not copies of any platform's questions.

items.title: Time-boxing
items.text: 15 minutes per problem, with a rule for when to move on, and a final pass for checks
The solving routine from the coding track, and the check() helper

items.title: Pattern recognition for each set
items.text: windows and dates (first and second event, monthly retention, gaps and islands); joins and complex types (relational division, date-range price join with explode, co-purchase recommendations); cleaning and cohorts (regex normalization, latest record per key, cohort pivot, skew-safe distinct counts and top-k)

items.title: The self-scoring log
items.text: finished in time, correct on first run, types matched, shuffle count, pattern name

blocks.label: Mock set A: windows and dates

items.text: purchases(user_id, ts, amount). For each user with at least two purchases, return the time between their first and second purchase.
logins(user_id, day). For each month, return the number of active users and the share of the previous month's users who were also active this month.
shifts(driver, shift_date, cancelled). For each driver, return the longest stretch of consecutive shifts with no cancellation, with its start and end dates.

blocks.label: Mock set B: joins and complex types

items.text: modules(course, module) and completions(student, module, completed_on). Per course, return the students who completed all its modules, with the date they finished the last one.

orders(order_id, ordered_on, items array<struct<sku, category, qty>>) and prices(sku, valid_from, valid_to, price). Price each item at its order date, give a 10 percent discount to one category, and return order totals.
purchases(customer, product). For each customer, return the top 3 products bought by other customers who share at least one product with them, excluding products they already own.

blocks.label: Mock set C: cleaning, aggregation and performance

items.text: customers(id, phone, updated_at) with phone numbers written many ways. Normalize them to digits only with a default country code, then keep the latest record per normalized phone.
signups(user_id, signup_date) and activity(user_id, day). Build a cohort table with signup month as rows and months since signup as columns, showing active user counts.
A heavily skewed events(country, user_id, page) table. Return distinct users per country and the top 3 pages per country, with no task in any stage taking more than 3 times the median task time.

activities.footnote: How to score yourself: for each problem, record whether you finished in time, whether it was correct on the first full run, whether the types matched the first time, the number of shuffles, and the pattern name from the cheat sheet. Any pattern that fails twice goes onto the next day's drill list.

items.text: A question bank built from the checklist, recording yourself, a rubric with four marks (mechanism, cost, trade-off, plan evidence)
Pick 20 checklist questions at random. Answer each aloud in 2 minutes while recording yourself, then replay it and mark every answer that missed a mechanism. Redo the weak ones.

activities.name: Self-test and log

items.text: you can walk through the capstone's plans end to end without notes, answer any checklist question in under 2 minutes, and finish each timed mock set within its 45 minutes. After this, run the same pipeline on a real cluster (managed Spark such as Databricks or EMR) to see multiple executors, real shuffles and real skew.

activities.footnote: After Day 15: solve one problem a day on your practice platform, and keep your log by pattern, not by problem. Redo every failed problem three days later from a blank file.
